questions.question: What is needed to transport hazardous materials?

options.text: Only a CDL.
A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.
A CDL with a tank endorsement.

questions.correctAnswerText: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.
questions.explanation: You need a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle that carries hazardous materials.

questions.question: If hazardous materials are leaking and the driver has no phone, what should they do?

options.text: Drive to find a phone and alert emergency personnel.
Drive to a hazardous materials clean-up facility.
Send someone else to get help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Send someone else to get help.
questions.explanation: Do not drive if cargo is leaking. Park your vehicle, secure it, stay with it, and contact emergency personnel. If you have no phone, send someone else to get help.

questions.question: What does a material's hazard class show?

options.text: The risks linked to the material.
How fast the material must be delivered.
How much the material weighs.

questions.correctAnswerText: The risks linked to the material.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials are sorted into nine classes. Each class explains the type of risks that come with the material.

questions.question: On shipping papers, should the identification number, shipping name, and hazard class be abbreviated?

options.text: Yes, if using small paper.
Yes, if the abbreviations are easy to understand.
No, never.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: The identification number, shipping name, and hazard class must never be abbreviated on hazardous materials shipping papers, unless the regulations specifically allow it.

questions.question: How should placards be placed on a vehicle?

options.text: Within three inches of other markings.
So words and numbers read from left to right.
Upside down.

questions.correctAnswerText: So words and numbers read from left to right.
questions.explanation: Placards must be placed at least three inches away from other markings. They must be level and positioned so words and numbers read from left to right.

questions.question: Who may transport hazardous materials?

options.text: Any driver with a CDL.
A driver with a CDL and hazardous materials endorsement.
Any driver in rural areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver with a CDL and hazardous materials endorsement.
questions.explanation: You must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle that carries hazardous materials.

questions.question: Where may hazardous materials shipping papers NOT be kept?

options.text: In a pouch on the driver's door.
In a pouch on the passenger's side door.
Within reach of the driver while the seat belt is fastened.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a pouch on the passenger's side door.
questions.explanation: Papers must be quick to reach in an emergency. While driving, keep papers in a pouch on the driver's door or in clear view within immediate reach. Papers may be on the driver's seat when the driver is not in the vehicle.

questions.question: What must a shipping paper include?

options.text: An emergency response telephone number.
The address of the shipper.
The location of fire departments along the route.

questions.correctAnswerText: An emergency response telephone number.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials shipping papers must include an emergency response telephone number.

questions.question: What should a driver check?

options.text: That shipping papers match package markings and labels.
That shipping papers are written in code.
That all packages are labeled as poison.

questions.correctAnswerText: That shipping papers match package markings and labels.
questions.explanation: Always compare package markings and labels to the shipping papers. Make sure the shipper listed the correct description and placed the correct labels on packages.

questions.question: If shipping papers list both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, what comes first?

options.text: The hazardous materials.
The non-hazardous materials.
Whichever has more weight.

questions.correctAnswerText: The hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials must be listed first on shipping papers that describe both hazardous and non-hazardous materials.

questions.question: What should you do if a hazardous materials label will not fit on the package?

options.text: Put the label on a tag that is securely attached to the package.
Attach a QR code to be scanned.
Make the HazMat label smaller so it fits on the package.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the label on a tag that is securely attached to the package.
questions.explanation: If a hazard warning label will not fit entirely on a package, you may place the label on a tag that is securely attached to the package instead.

questions.question: Where should a hazardous material's identification number appear?

options.text: On the vehicle's bumper.
On the material's package.
On a sticker near the shipping container.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the material's package.
questions.explanation: The ID number must appear on the shipping paper and on the package. It must also appear on cargo tanks and other large containers.

questions.question: What is true about shipping papers for hazardous materials?

options.text: They are not needed for most shipments.
They are required for all shipments.
They can be stored only in digital files.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are required for all shipments.
questions.explanation: Shippers of hazardous materials must provide shipping papers to explain the risks of the materials.

questions.question: When loading a compressed gas tank, the liquid discharge valves should be:

options.text: Closed.
Removed.
Opened.

questions.correctAnswerText: Opened.
questions.explanation: Liquid discharge valves on a compressed gas tank must be kept closed at all times, except during loading and unloading.

questions.question: What shape is a hazardous materials placard?

options.text: Diamond
Triangle
Circle

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond
questions.explanation: Vehicles carrying hazardous materials must display diamond-shaped warning signs on all four sides. These signs are called placards.

questions.question: How should a shipper warn others when transporting hazardous materials?

options.text: Display HazMat placards on the truck.
Use flashing lights on the truck.
Sound a siren.

questions.correctAnswerText: Display HazMat placards on the truck.
questions.explanation: Shippers must display diamond-shaped warning signs, called placards, on vehicles carrying certain hazardous materials. Shippers must also provide labels, shipping papers, and emergency response information.

questions.question: What is the correct way to check tire pressure?

options.text: Use a tire pressure gauge.
Look at the tire.
Push on the tire to feel the pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a tire pressure gauge.
questions.explanation: Check each tire at the start of each trip. A tire pressure gauge is the only way to accurately check tire pressure.

questions.question: What could indicate that cargo contains hazardous materials?

options.text: The cargo is stored in cylinder tanks.
The cargo is picked up from a supermarket.
The cargo is on wooden pallets.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cargo is stored in cylinder tanks.
questions.explanation: Cylinders and drums are commonly used to hold hazardous materials. Take proper safety steps when transporting hazardous materials.

questions.question: Which agency helps coordinate emergency response to chemical hazards?

options.text: The National Response Center
The Federal Containment Organization
The United Center for Chemical Assistance

questions.correctAnswerText: The National Response Center
questions.explanation: The National Response Center helps coordinate emergency response to chemical hazards. Contact it if there is a hazardous materials spill.

questions.question: What is a sign that your shipment may contain hazardous materials?

options.text: The shipper sells fireworks or munitions.
Your last shipment was labeled as hazardous.
The packaging looks damaged.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipper sells fireworks or munitions.
questions.explanation: One sign that a shipment may contain hazardous materials is the type of business of the shipper. Examples include paint dealers, chemical suppliers, pest control businesses, agricultural suppliers, and fireworks or munitions dealers.

questions.question: If hazardous materials catch fire while you are transporting them, what should you do?

options.text: Try to put out the fire with a fire extinguisher.
Call emergency personnel and let them handle the fire.
Hope the fire goes out on its own.

questions.correctAnswerText: Call emergency personnel and let them handle the fire.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials fires need special training and protective equipment. Do not try to fight a hazardous materials fire yourself unless you have proper training and equipment.

questions.question: When transporting Division 1.3 materials, what kind of floor liner should be used?

options.text: Non-ferrous materials.
Metallic materials.
Loosely attached materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Non-ferrous materials.
questions.explanation: Use a floor liner when transporting Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 materials. The floor must be tight and the liner must be non-metallic or non-ferrous metal. Non-ferrous metals do not contain iron.

questions.question: What should a driver do if given a leaking package of hazardous materials?

options.text: Accept it.
Refuse it.
Leave it on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Refuse it.
questions.explanation: Drivers must refuse to transport any package or shipment of hazardous materials that is leaking.

questions.question: Where should shipping papers be placed in the cab?

options.text: Hidden from view.
In the glove box.
In a place where anyone entering the cab can easily see them.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a place where anyone entering the cab can easily see them.
questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers in a pouch on the driver's side door or in another location the driver can easily reach while wearing a seat belt. They must be clearly visible to anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: When transporting explosives, what is required?

options.text: You must have a written route plan.
You should take the shortest possible route.
You can always use tunnels.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must have a written route plan.
questions.explanation: When transporting Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, you must follow a written route plan. Avoid heavily populated areas, crowds, tunnels, narrow streets, and alleys. Check for any route restrictions.

questions.question: How must a hazardous waste manifest be signed?

options.text: By hand.
Electronically.
Attached to the outside of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: By hand.
questions.explanation: When transporting hazardous waste, you must carry a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest. It must be signed by hand.

questions.question: Class 1, Class 2.1, and Class 3 materials should not be transported in a trailer with:

options.text: A heater.
An air conditioner.
Other items.

questions.correctAnswerText: A heater.
questions.explanation: Cargo heaters are not always allowed. When transporting Class 1 (Explosives), Class 2.1 (Flammable Gases), or Class 3 (Flammable Liquids), heaters in the same space are generally prohibited.

questions.question: Where can you find identification numbers for hazardous chemicals?

options.text: In the DOT Emergency Response Guide.
In the truck's driver's manual.
On the company's website.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the DOT Emergency Response Guide.
questions.explanation: The U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) Emergency Response Guide provides information about hazardous materials. It is indexed by proper shipping names and hazardous materials identification numbers.

questions.question: When can an improperly placarded vehicle be moved?

options.text: To make room for other vehicles.
Only in an emergency.
If it will travel fewer than 10 miles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only in an emergency.
questions.explanation: An improperly placarded vehicle may only be driven when it is necessary to protect life or property in an emergency.

questions.question: When transporting hazardous materials, how should placards be displayed?

options.text: They should be lit up.
They should be used on all four sides of the vehicle.
They should be used only by Class A licensed drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should be used on all four sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be placed on all four sides of a vehicle when required.
